text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests that measure your blood glucose or average blood sugar levels over time.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests that measure your blood glucose or average blood sugar levels over time

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar level over the past 2 to 3 months.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after fasting (no food or drink except water) for at least 8 hours.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar 2 hours after you drink a special sugary liquid.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures your blood sugar at any time of day, used if you are showing classic diabetes symptoms (such as extreme thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained weight loss).

text_blocks.snippet: In most cases without severe symptoms, doctors will repeat the diagnostic test on a second day to confirm the results. More detailed guidelines and patient resources are available through the American Diabetes Association and the U.S. National Library of Medicine.
